I applied light machine grease and the pulley turned much freer but was still tight. I reassembled the dryer and the noise is gone. The part was inexpensive and thanks to youtube, I was able to learn how to replace the part myself saving an expensive service call.

Fit as advertised, I had to remove the back pannel that had about a dozen or more screws. Then removed 1 bolt that held the bracket and pulley. There is a tension spring that keeps the pressure and the pulley on tight. there is a plastic triangle that keeps the pulley on and a round plastic washer between the pulley and bracket. The old worn out pulley came off easy enough. It's a very tight fit to get the bushing (not a bearing) on to the bracket, I used a large pair of channel locks and slowly sqweezed it on to the bracket. The hardest part of the part replacement was the tension spring,after the bracket is bolted back on and the belt on, get the tension spring back on.. I was trying with needle nosed pliers and the darn spring kept turning right before I could get it lined up. My solution was to us a small pair of vise-grips to lock on to the bottom of the spring and stretch it to fit in at the bottom.

YouTube has how to videos if you search for them.

The price was right, but the product, not so much. This Blue Stars replacement idler pulley lasted just over 6 months and then exploded apart. The product description says "Ultra Durable" which has proven to be incorrect in my experience, as 6 months is no where near ultra durable.

It also says "Exact Fit for Whirlpool & Kenmore dryer" which is not accurate. It did not fit well on the shaft of my Kenmore dryer, and yes it was the correct replacement part for my model. It took force and effort to get it in place. Then it began to squeal right from the start, and operated loudly when it wasn't an all on squeal. As it approached its end, it squealed loudly and regularly, signifying its imminent demise.

As a dryer repair like this is a bit of a job, this time I searched for better parts and found a genuine Whirlpool part to replace this one. It was more expensive but reasonable and, I think, worth every penny. It slid on the shaft properly and easily, and the dryer sounds quieter than it has in ages.

The quality of the product was good, but it did not appear to be the direct replacement for the original pulley.  It was larger OD by approximately 1/4".  The original slid off the shaft easily, but the replacement was a heavy interference fit.  I had to lubricate the shaft and tap the new pulley into place where it stopped 1/2 way on.  When attempting remove the stuck replacement pulley off the shaft, the plastic pulley separated from its metal hub.  I used channel locks against the end of the hub and the backside of the bracket to move the hub into proper position.  Once in position I installed the plastic pulley onto the hub.  It turned very tight, but once I put the belt back in place and started the drier it ran fine and the squealing was gone. My rating would have been higher but for the difficulty in installation.  It turned a 10 minute job into 70 minutes.
